rows.label: Marketplace:
rows.text: ==Three-sided==: customers, restaurants, delivery partners; own app and SLA each.

rows.label: Aggregator:
rows.text: Lists restaurants, does **not** cook, takes 20-30% commission.

items: ==Hyperlocal==: 5-8 km radius, partition by **city**
==Perishable==: 40-minute SLA beats throughput
==Peaky==: lunch 12-2 pm, dinner 7-10 pm, ~60% of orders

rows: No warehouse stock; hourly menus; live logistics

blocks.title: Ask first (clarifying questions)
items: Which cities at launch?
Vegetarian-only mode?
Scheduled orders?
Cash on delivery?

blocks.title: INTERVIEW TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: ~40-minute delivery across three parties, per city, peaking at lunch and dinner, drives the design.

rows: view menu, build cart, apply coupon, place order, pay
track live, get status alerts, cancel, rate
accept or reject order, mark ready

items: **Strong** consistency: orders and payments
**Eventual** consistency: menu, search, ratings
A stale menu is fine; a double charge is not

blocks.text: 300K riders each ping every 4 s, so ==75K writes/s== hit the tracking path, about 300x the order rate.

blocks.title: DESIGN TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: Reads are 100x writes; location writes are 300x orders. Size search for 25K QPS and tracking for 75K writes/s.

slides.page_title: Layers, Data Stores and Request Flow

rows.label: Clients:
rows.text: customer app, restaurant tablet, rider app, ops dashboard

rows.label: Edge:
rows.text: ==CDN== for images and menus; ==API gateway== for auth, rate limits, routing

rows.label: Core services:
rows.text: Search, Catalog, Cart, Order, Payment, Dispatch, Tracking, Notification

rows.label: Calls:
rows.text: **REST** at the edge, **gRPC** between services, Kafka for async

blocks.title: Data rules
items: ==Database per service==: nobody reads another's tables
**Shard by city**: supply, demand, failures stay local
Order path is ==synchronous== up to payment
Everything after payment is **event-driven** on Kafka
`OrderPlaced`, `PaymentCaptured`, `OrderAccepted`
`RiderAssigned`, `Delivered`

slides.subtitle: (Food Delivery App)

items: Supply is bound to a ==5-8 km== radius
A city outage stays **local**
Each city scales for its own peak

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.text: Say "start modular, split along order, payment, dispatch" in interviews.

blocks.title: INTERVIEW TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: Start modular, keep payment synchronous, make everything after it events, and shard by city.

blocks.title: 1. Responsibilities
items: List ==nearby open restaurants== for the user's location
Search by **dish** or cuisine, e.g. 'biryani'
Filter the results, then rank them
Serve all of it at 25K QPS, p99 300 ms

rows: tags for dish and cuisine match

items: Geo filter runs **first**: it shrinks candidates before text match
Border restaurants need the ==neighbour cells== too
Closed or out-of-zone restaurants are dropped, not ranked

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.text: In interviews, say "geo first, text second, rank last" to explain the query order.

blocks.title: 6. Idempotency and Consistency
items: Kafka ==CDC== from the catalog DB updates the index in **under 5 s**
Open or closed lives in ==Redis==, not in the index
Cursor paging stays stable while the index changes
Card details come from cache, so a read has no side effects

blocks.title: 7. Failure Scenarios
items: **Stale index** shows a closed restaurant: re-check availability at cart time
**ES down**: fall back to a ==Redis top-N== by geohash
Neighbour cells skipped: border restaurants vanish from results

blocks.title: 8. Events and Metrics
items: Consumes catalog CDC events from Kafka
Search **p99 300 ms**; zero-result rate under **3%**
Search-to-order conversion; index lag in seconds

blocks.title: 9. Design Considerations
items: ✓ Rank on distance, rating, ETA, popularity, conversion, ==personalization==
✓ Autocomplete: prefix index plus fuzzy, so 'pizzaa' still finds pizza
✓ One index per city keeps shards small and queries local

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.text: Say "stale index is fine, stale cart is not": re-check open status at checkout.

items: Store **restaurants**, menus, items and prices
Hold ==variants== and ==availability== per item
Read to write ratio is about ==1000:1==
Serve reads from cache and CDN, **60 s** TTL
Hierarchy: Restaurant → Category → Item → VariantGroup → Addon
Stock-out is a ==fast toggle== that skips the full publish
Order keeps a **price snapshot**: item name and price at order time

blocks.title: Why snapshot the price?
items: Menus change by the ==hour==, orders must not
Order history shows what was **actually** charged
Refunds and disputes use the snapshot, not the live menu

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.text: Say "cache the menu, toggle the stock": 1000:1 reads, but sold-out must be instant.

slides.page_title: Menu Data Model, APIs and Metrics

blocks.title: Money rule
blocks.text: Store **integer paise**, never floats: 0.1 + 0.2 breaks totals.

items: Item sold out **after** it was added to the cart
Re-validate every item at checkout
Show a ==substitution prompt== instead of failing the order
Alert when the item-unavailable rate spikes

blocks.title: TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: Cache menus hard, but toggle stock fast and check the menu_version at checkout.

slides.subtitle: Food Delivery App

items: ==Hold== the selected items, apply offers, compute fees
Validate the cart, then hand off to the **Order** service
{icon:redis} Redis hash keyed by `user_id`, ==24 h TTL==, not durable
**One restaurant** per cart: a new restaurant prompts to clear it
Coupon rules: ==min order value==, first-order-only, per-user limit, validity window
Delivery fee depends on distance, demand and weather
The quoted fee is **locked** into the order

rows: uses so far under the cap

blocks.title: Why Redis for carts?
items: Carts are ==ephemeral==: losing one is cheap
Hash ops are **fast** for add, change, remove
TTL cleans abandoned carts for free

blocks.title: Quote lock
blocks.text: The price quote is valid for **5 minutes**; after that, reprice.

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.text: Say "cart is ephemeral, the order is durable" to justify Redis here.

items: Client sends an ==idempotency key== per checkout
Order service stores key with a unique index
A double tap on Place Order returns the **same** order
Price changed between cart and pay: show a ==diff==, require **re-confirm**
Never silently charge more than the quote
Restaurant closed at checkout: block with a clear message
Quote older than 5 min: reprice and quote again
Cart-to-order conversion about ==30%==
Checkout p99 under ==800 ms==
Coupon failure rate, tracked per code
Cart abandonment rate, carts expiring at 24 h

blocks.title: INTERVIEW TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: Cart is ephemeral Redis; the 5-minute quote and idempotency key make checkout safe.

blocks.title: 1. Responsibilities
items: Be the **single source of truth** for an order's lifecycle
Coordinate Payment, Dispatch and Notification, so no other service owns order status

blocks.title: Child tables
items: `OrderItem`(order_id, item_id, qty, price_snapshot)
`OrderEvent`(order_id, from, to, actor, ts): audit log

blocks.title: 6. Idempotency and Consistency
items: A retried POST with the same key returns the **same order**
Optimistic lock: `UPDATE ... WHERE id=? AND version=?`
0 rows updated means another actor won: reload, retry
Outbox: DB write and Kafka event commit in **one transaction**

blocks.title: 7. Failure Scenarios
items: Restaurant silent for 3 minutes: auto-REJECTED, then refund
Stuck PAYMENT_PENDING: timeout job sweeps it at 15 minutes
Saga step fails: Order service compensates with refund and rider release

blocks.title: 8. Events Published
items: OrderPlaced, OrderAccepted, OrderCancelled, OrderDelivered
Sent by the outbox relay, keyed by `order_id`

blocks.title: 9. Key Metrics
items: Order success rate above **98%**
Acceptance time p50 **40 s**
Cancellation rate, split by reason
Orchestration keeps the whole saga in ==one owner==
Snapshot price and address so history never shifts
Log every transition in `OrderEvent` with its actor
Never delete an order: end it in a terminal state

blocks.title: 1. Responsibilities
items: **Charge**, refund and reconcile; keep state correct across PSPs
Methods: UPI, cards, wallets, net banking, cash on delivery
Never store raw card numbers: use a ==PCI-compliant gateway== and tokenization

blocks.title: 5. Key APIs
items: `POST /payments` carries an ==idempotency key==
`POST /payments/{id}/refund` starts a refund
`POST /webhooks/psp` receives PSP events

blocks.title: 6. Idempotency and Consistency
items: Webhook: verify the **signature** first
Deduplicate by event id, process idempotently
Never trust the client redirect
Only a webhook or status poll confirms success

blocks.title: 7. Failure Scenarios
items: User debited, webhook lost: reconciler polls PENDING every **2 min**
Money is moved by the PSP; we keep a ==double-entry ledger==
Gateway A success rate under 90%: route new payments to B

blocks.title: 8. Events Published
items: `PaymentCaptured` on SUCCESS
`PaymentFailed` on FAILED
`RefundCompleted` on REFUNDED

blocks.title: 9. Key Metrics
items: Payment success rate above **95%**
p99 PSP latency under 2 s (estimate)
Pending-payment age under 5 min
Daily reconciliation mismatches: target **0**
Tokenize cards; raw numbers never touch our servers
Store money as integer paise, never floats
Fail over to the backup PSP on low success rate
Cash on delivery skips the PSP but still hits the ledger

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.text: Say "the webhook is the truth, the redirect is a hint" in interviews.

items: Find a rider for **every** accepted order
Minimize ==wait and delivery time== for customer and restaurant
Balance load so no rider is starved or overloaded
Trigger: dispatch starts at restaurant acceptance, timed so the rider arrives when the food is ready
Candidates: online, {green:IDLE} riders within 3 km via geohash
Score: pickup distance, rating, load, direction, prep time
Greedy: nearest rider, simple; **batched** Hungarian every 10 s, better
Bundle 2 orders: same restaurant or same direction
Offer: 20 s timer, rider 1 then 2, 3 attempts, then widen radius

slides.page_title: Dispatch Locks, Metrics and Matching Trade-offs

items: Two dispatchers offer one rider: an ==atomic Redis lock== stops it
Rider drops off mid-order: **re-assign** the order and free the rider
Offer times out: the next-best rider gets it, up to 3 tries
Assignment time: **p50 30 s**
Offer acceptance: above ==70%==
Rider idle time: tracked per city, minimized
Start dispatch early so the rider is not waiting at the restaurant
Widen the radius only after ==3 failed offers==
Lock the rider **before** sending the offer

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.text: Say "batch every 10 s for better matches, lock before you offer" in interviews.

blocks.title: TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: Dispatch from acceptance, score nearby riders, match in batches, and lock every offer.

slides.subtitle: (Food Delivery App)

blocks.title: 1. Responsibilities
items: Ingest rider locations and show **live position** + ETA
Rider app pings GPS every ==4 s== on a trip
Batches pings; slows down when idle (no order)
Customer sees the dot move and a live ETA

blocks.title: 3. Storage and push
items: Hot: Redis GEO keeps ==only the latest== position per rider
Cold: Cassandra history, **30-day** TTL
Push over WebSocket or SSE; fallback: poll every **5 s**
Fan-out is cheap: 1 rider = 1 watcher, no celebrity problem

blocks.title: Tip
blocks.text: Say "hot is the latest ping, cold is history, push to the one watcher" in interviews.

slides.page_title: ETA, Location Data Model and Failures

blocks.title: 5. ETA and smoothing
items: ETA = rider→restaurant + ==remaining prep== + restaurant→customer
Routing engine like **OSRM** plus live traffic
Map matching snaps GPS onto roads
Drop any jump over **100 km/h** as noise

blocks.title: 7. Key APIs
items: `POST /rider/location` (batched pings)
`GET /orders/{id}/track` (poll fallback)
`WS /track/{order_id}` (live push)

blocks.title: 8. Failures and metrics
items: Rider in a tunnel: show last position + **reconnecting**
Extrapolate the ETA while offline
Location-to-screen lag under ==5 s==
WebSocket connections about **1M**; ETA error under 3 min at p90

blocks.title: TAKEAWAY:
blocks.text: Keep only the latest ping hot, push it to the one watcher, and stay honest when the signal drops.

How would you design Swiggy for millions of orders? 🍔🛵

This is the system design interview question that trips up most candidates. So here's the whole answer, as handwritten notes you can swipe through.

What's inside, in order:

📌 Problem statement and scope
📊 Requirements and scale estimates
🏗️ High-level architecture
🔍 Restaurant discovery and search
📋 Menu and catalog service
🛒 Cart and checkout
📦 Order service and state machine
💳 Payments
🛵 Delivery partner assignment
📍 Real-time tracking
🔔 Notifications
⚖️ Scaling and failure handling
✅ A one-page cheatsheet to revise before the interview

It closes with the trade-offs and interview questions that interviewers actually ask.
